title: Data-Driven Loss Functions for Inference-Time Optimization in Text-to-Image (Learn-to-Steer)
property: spatial relation between two objects (above, below, left of, right of)
reads: All L x H cross-attention maps of the subject word and of the object word, plus the timestep; the relation word's own map is not an input
trained_on: Inverted real GQA and synthetic images (Flux 20K+4K, SD 4K+4K), each inverted under the correct and a random wrong relation, both labelled with the true relation; cross-entropy
gradient_enters: Latent update z_t <- z_t - alpha grad L_t with L_t = -log p[r], first 50% of steps, alpha 5 (SD 2.1, Flux) or 7.5 (SD 1.4), 15 iterations per step, no stated cap
unseen: yes: 16 object categories absent from training (6 from T2I-CompBench, 10 from ChatGPT), 200 prompts, 0.60 on FLUX.1-dev; chosen as absent words rather than by a planned split, near relatives such as corgi and tiger possible (inferred)
headline: GenEval position (fraction of 400 images with correct relation, 0 to 1, higher better): vanilla to Learn-to-Steer 0.07 to 0.54 on SD 2.1 (COMPASS 0.51) and 0.20 to 0.61 on FLUX.1-dev (COMPASS 0.60); on 16 unseen categories 0.60 on FLUX.1-dev (vanilla 0.18, COMPASS 0.58)
copy_or_avoid: Copy the wrong-word inversion check and two-inversion training; hold out whole families, add a fused label, and test dose because it uses 15 uncapped iterations per step (inferred)

quotes.text: The classifier predicts p̂ = C(As , Ao , t), where p̂ is the predicted probability distribution over relation classes
quotes.supports: reads: inputs are the two object map sets and the timestep

quotes.text: For a given object, the aggregator receives all L × H attention maps of size h × w.
quotes.supports: reads: all layers and heads per word

quotes.text: The inputs to the relation classifier are the cross-attention maps of two objects, alongside the current denoising
For Flux-based models, we use 20K real images from GQA and 4K synthetic images.
with a balanced mixture of 4K real and 4K synthetic images
we perform inversion twice: once with a "mismatching" prompt that correctly describes the spatial relation
and once with a prompt containing a randomly sampled incorrect relation
both sets of extracted attention maps are labeled with the ground-truth relation observed in the image
quotes.supports: trained_on: both inversions carry the true label

quotes.text: the classifier detected subtle traces of the relation word ("left") encoded within the maps
quotes.supports: claim 5: first classifier learned traces of the relation word

quotes.text: compute a cross-entropy loss against the desired relation r from the prompt: Lt = − log p̂[r]
update the latent code with its gradient: zt ← zt − α∇zt Lt . We optimize the first 50% of the denoising steps.
The step size α is 5 for SD2.1 and Flux-based models, and 7.5 for SD1.4 and number of optimization iterations per step are 15.
uses 200 prompts across 16 object categories unseen by both our method and COMPASS
Only 6 categories from T2ICompBench were external to both methods, and 10 additional categories were proposed by ChatGPT
